description: Official US facts about a car, truck or SUV from a VIN or a year, make and model: specs decoded from the VIN (NHTSA vPIC), recalls (NHTSA), owner complaints with the most-reported problem areas, NHTSA 5-star crash ratings, and EPA fuel economy (fueleconomy.gov). Add miles (you work out the distance) for the exact fuel cost of a drive: the car's EPA combined mpg (or an mpg the person gives) times this week's average pump price from the US Energy Information Administration for the state, its region or the US. Use when someone owns, is buying or is comparing a vehicle, used or new, and for road trips, commutes and 'is it cheaper to drive or fly'. A VIN gives the exact version; without one, results cover the model year. Doesn't show accident history, title status or value.

fuel.description: For fuel cost, when the model comes in both

fuel_only.description: true when only fuel cost is wanted; skips recall, complaint and crash-rating lookups (needs miles and mpg, or year/make/model)

miles.description: For fuel cost: driving distance in miles, one way

mpg.description: For fuel cost: the car's mpg, if known or when there's no specific car

round_trip.description: For fuel cost: true to double the distance

state.description: For fuel cost: two-letter US state where most of the driving happens, e.g. CA

year.description: Model year, when there's no VIN

name: check_car
title: Car: official facts about a vehicle, and fuel cost
